{{Short description|English mathematician (1590-1682)}}
{{About other people|the mathematician|Richard White|Richard White (disambiguation){{!}}Richard White}}
[[File:White - Hemisphaerium dissectum, 1648 - 849329 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Title page of the 1648 ''Hemisphaerium Dissectum'']]

'''Richard White''' ({{langx|la|Ricardus Albius}}; 1590 – 1682) was an English [[mathematician]] and [[physicist]].

A [[Catholic Church|Catholic]] from [[Essex]], he studied under [[Benedetto Castelli]] in [[Pisa]] and lived mostly in [[Italy]]. His brother, [[Thomas White (scholar)|Thomas White]] was a Roman Catholic theologian and scholar. He married Catherine Weston, daughter of the [[Richard Weston, 1st Earl of Portland|Earl of Portland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://catalogues.royalsociety.org/CalmView/Record.aspx?src=CalmView.Persons&id=NA405|title=Record. White; Richard (fl 1661)|work=royalsociety.org}}</ref> 

In the preface of his book ''Hemisphaerium Dissectum'', printed in [[Rome]] with the [[Inquisition]]'s permission, he wrote with great admiration of [[Galileo Galilei]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Catalogue of the Mathematical, Historical and Miscellaneous Portion of the Celebrated Library of M. Guglielmo Libri|volume=2|publisher=S. Leigh Sotheby & John Wilkinson|year=1861|page=791|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AW0BNIjfOfIC&pg=PA791}}</ref> He also had with Galileo a friendly correspondence by letter.<ref>{{Cite book|first=Antonio|last=Favaro|title=Amici e corrispondenti di Galileo Galilei|location=Venice|publisher=Carlo Ferrari|year=1894|pages=16–17|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=s0-G2BZ9y4gC&pg=RA16-PA16|language=it}}</ref>

White was proposed for election to the [[Royal Society|Philosophical Society]] in June 1661, and was elected on 26 June 1661. However, he was not re-elected after the second charter in 1663 and is not listed as an original fellow of the Royal Society.<ref>{{cite journal|title=The Earliest Fellows of the Royal Society|last=de Beer|first=
E. S.|journal=Notes and Records of the Royal Society of London|volume=7|year=1950|pages=172-192|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/531317}}</ref>
